title: When the Will Falls
premise: Paloma Blackwood, archivist of St. Verity's Cathedral, discovers the diary of Sister Anselm—a nun who vanished thirty years ago—hidden in the locked crypt's records, and finds entries written after her disappearance. As Paloma decodes the diary's coded final pages, she learns Anselm witnessed a murder tied to the cathedral's founding will, a bequest that still pays the diocese's debts and whose statute of limitations expires in weeks. The suspects are now pillars of the community: the bishop, the estate lawyer, and Paloma's own mentor, Canon Ives, whose alibi was woven with the others three decades ago. When Paloma is attacked in the crypt and the diary pages begin vanishing from the archive, she realizes the killer has been guarding the secret all along—and that Anselm may have died protecting someone she loved. In the climax beneath the crypt floor, Paloma confronts Canon Ives, who confesses he covered up the death of the original testator's heir to preserve the will and the cathedral itself; Anselm, who loved him, chose exile over exposure and lived out her days writing to no one. The will falls—voided by fraud—but the truth finally sets both the dead and the living free.
about_author: Felix Reyes spent a decade cataloguing ecclesiastical archives across the American Southwest before turning to fiction full-time. His mysteries draw on real archival oddities—sealed crypts, amended wills, and the quiet violence of institutional memory.

chapters.title: The Locked Crypt
chapters.summary: Paloma Blackwood, POV. During a routine inventory of St. Verity's restricted archive, Paloma catalogs the sealed crypt access ledger and notes an entry dated after its last official opening. The chapter establishes her devotion to the cathedral and her unease with what institutions choose to forget. Emotional beat: quiet dread beneath professional calm.

chapters.title: A Diary That Outlived Its Author
chapters.summary: Paloma, POV. Tucked inside a misfiled deed box, she finds Sister Anselm's diary—the missing nun who vanished in 1995. The final entry is dated eleven months after her disappearance. Paloma reads it twice, hands shaking, then locks it in her desk instead of reporting it. Emotional beat: fascination curdling into fear.

chapters.title: Thirty Years of Alibis
chapters.summary: Paloma, POV. She pulls the old disappearance file: every witness gave the same tidy account of the night Anselm left—Canon Ives, Bishop Ferrar, lawyer Marcus Deloach. Identical phrasing, down to the hour. Paloma begins a private timeline on butcher paper in her flat. Emotional beat: the thrill of a pattern emerging.

chapters.title: What the Will Pays For
chapters.summary: Paloma, POV. Researching the Blackwood-adjacent founding will (her own family name appears as witnesses), she learns the cathedral's endowment hinges on a bequest contingent on the heir's death being 'natural and unmolested.' If fraud voids it, the diocese collapses. Emotional beat: dawning conflict between truth and loyalty.

chapters.title: Canon Ives Remembers Everything
chapters.summary: Paloma, POV. She probes her mentor gently over tea; Ives answers too smoothly, quoting dates verbatim, then warns her off 'old griefs.' A moment of warmth between them sours. Emotional beat: betrayal anticipated but not yet confirmed.

chapters.title: Entry After the End
chapters.summary: Anselm, POV (diary excerpts interleaved with Paloma reading). The post-disappearance entries reveal Anselm alive, hiding, watching the cathedral, writing in code about 'the second grave.' Paloma cross-references the code against hymn numbers. Emotional beat: intimacy with a voice from the past.

chapters.title: The Statute Clock
chapters.summary: Paloma, POV. A retired detective, Ruth Okonkwo, tells her the estate-fraud statute expires in five weeks; after that, no one can ever be charged. Ruth agrees to help unofficially. They map which alibi breaks first. Emotional beat: urgency sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: Deloach's Paper Trail
chapters.summary: Paloma, POV. She visits estate lawyer Marcus Deloach, now semi-retired, and finds his 1995 files suspiciously complete—too complete, rehearsed. He mentions Anselm's name unprompted. That night, someone searches Paloma's office. Emotional beat: hunter realizing she is hunted.

chapters.title: The Second Grave
chapters.summary: Paloma, POV. Decoded diary pages point to a burial beneath the crypt's oldest bay. With Ruth, she enters at night and finds disturbed ground under the flagstones—and fresh boot prints leaving. Emotional beat: awe and terror in equal measure.

chapters.title: Bishop Ferrar's Confession of Silence
chapters.summary: Paloma, POV. The dying bishop, pressed by Paloma, admits he knew something happened in 1995 but was told the will—and four hundred jobs—depended on silence. He gives her a key to Deloach's old strongbox. Emotional beat: pity for complicity without absolution.

chapters.title: Pages Missing
chapters.summary: Paloma, POV. Three diary pages vanish from her locked desk; only Ives and one volunteer had keys. Paloma lies to police about the diary's existence, crossing her own line. Emotional beat: guilt of becoming a keeper of secrets herself.

chapters.title: Anselm's Love Letters
chapters.summary: Anselm, POV. Undecoded marginalia reveals Anselm loved someone inside the conspiracy—initials C.I. Her entries wrestle between exposing the crime and protecting him. Paloma reads this alone at 3 a.m., weeping. Emotional beat: heartbreak across time.

chapters.title: The Volunteer
chapters.summary: Paloma, POV. The archive volunteer, Tomas, is found to be Deloach's grandson, planted to watch the files. Confronted, he breaks: his grandfather confessed on his deathbed that the heir's death was no accident. Emotional beat: the past reaching into the next generation.

chapters.title: Ruth Pulls the Old File
chapters.summary: Ruth, POV. The ex-detective reopens her memory of the 1995 case she was ordered to close. She finds the coroner's report was altered—one signature forged. She tells Paloma: whoever forged it had authority. Emotional beat: institutional rot made personal.

chapters.title: Ives Asks Her to Stop
chapters.summary: Paloma, POV. Ives comes to her flat at night—not threatening, pleading. He speaks of the cathedral as a living body that must not bleed out. He nearly confesses, then retreats. Paloma realizes he loves her like a daughter, which makes it worse. Emotional beat: love against duty, embodied.

chapters.title: The Strongbox
chapters.summary: Paloma and Ruth, alternating POV. Using the bishop's key, they open Deloach's strongbox: the true coroner's page, a photograph of the heir alive after his 'death' date, and Anselm's last letter, unmailed. The letter names the killer. Emotional beat: the trap snapping shut.

chapters.title: Vespers for the Dead
chapters.summary: Paloma, POV. She attends evening service watching Ives across the choir, knowing what the letter says: Ives struck the heir in panic during a dispute over the will, and the others buried it—literally—to save the church. Anselm saw everything. Emotional beat: grief preceding confrontation.

chapters.title: Beneath the Flagstones
chapters.summary: Paloma, POV. Lured by a forged note in Ives' hand, she descends into the crypt at night. Ives appears; the confrontation turns physical as he tries to take the letter. Ruth arrives; Ives collapses, confessing all—the strike, the burial, the alibis, and letting Anselm flee rather than die. Emotional beat: climax, raw and human.

chapters.title: Where Anselm Went
chapters.summary: Paloma, POV. Following the letter's instructions, they trace Anselm to a convent hospice record: she died peacefully in 2011 under another name, having written her diary 'to leave a door open for whoever came looking.' Emotional beat: sorrow transfigured into tenderness.

chapters.title: The Will Falls
chapters.summary: Paloma, POV. The evidence voids the bequest; the diocese must sell land and shrink, parishes rage, and Ives is charged within the statute's final days. Paloma testifies, voice steady, heart breaking. Emotional beat: cost of truth counted honestly.

chapters.title: Requiem in the Archive
chapters.summary: Paloma, POV. Months later, the crypt is opened properly and the heir's remains laid to rest; Anselm's diary is accessioned into the public archive under her true name. Ives, awaiting trial, sends Paloma a letter of blessing she cannot yet answer. Emotional beat: mourning with integrity.

chapters.title: What Paloma Keeps
chapters.summary: Paloma, POV. Standing in the unlocked crypt, sunlight through the grate, Paloma chooses to stay as archivist—not to guard secrets, but to keep doors open. She writes the first entry in a new ledger: the truth, plainly stated. Emotional beat: resolution, quiet and earned.
